phases.message: I'm Calla Rourke. Our home was flooded and FEMA has decided our requests. Start in Reliefmoor: read the rules, our registration and every page of FEMA's decisions with the last day to appeal each. Read, and do not appeal anything yet.
Hearthguard is our insurer. Read what it paid on our claim, line by line.
Lenswick has our photos, estimates and receipts. Read every page and note what each one is.
Postwren is my mail. Read every page, the old letters too, and note what each attachment is. Don't reply to anyone.

Back in Reliefmoor, appeal to FEMA, inside the 60 days, each decision that the rules say is wrong, for the amount that insurance left unpaid or that FEMA did not pay, with a written explanation naming the documents. Appeal nothing the rules do not allow, and don't reply to anyone. Then tell me, for each decision, whether you appealed, for how much and why, and what you left alone.

ihp_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Reliefmoor is the Rourke household's applicant page for the Harrowmere Valley floods (an invented declaration, DR-9017, declared 17 July 2026 with Individual Assistance). The rules below are FEMA's, as 44 CFR 206.110 to 206.120, with the Individual Assistance rule in force since 22 March 2024, and FEMA's Individual Assistance Program and Policy Guide state them. Topics: appeal, insurance, covered, ineligible, maximum.

44 CFR 206.115: an applicant may appeal a FEMA decision in writing within 60 days after the date FEMA notifies the applicant, which is the date on the decision letter. The appeal needs a written explanation or verifiable documentation, signed by the applicant. FEMA answers in writing within 90 days, and its decision on the appeal is final. Reliefmoor shows each decision's letter date and the last day to appeal.

Stafford Act section 312 and 44 CFR 206.191: insurance comes first. FEMA pays for an eligible loss only what insurance did not, and may not duplicate it. An applicant with insurance gives FEMA the settlement letter or the denial before that part is decided. What the policy's limits leave unpaid is an unmet need FEMA can consider.

44 CFR 206.113, 206.117 and 206.119: repair assistance covers the structure of an owner-occupied primary residence, its windows and doors, heating and air conditioning, utility systems and interior parts, to a safe and sanitary condition, where the damage is not covered by insurance. Other needs assistance covers personal property, transportation (vehicle repair or replacement), medical and dental, funeral, moving and storage, and other necessary expenses, for an applicant whose primary residence was damaged.

44 CFR 206.113(b): housing help is for the pre-disaster primary residence, not a second or vacation home. Anything not authorized by 206.117 and 206.119 is excluded, which leaves out landscaping and fencing. Business losses are excluded. A household that has been paid by insurance for a loss is not paid for it again.

For a disaster declared in fiscal year 2026 (on or after 1 October 2025) the most FEMA can give one household is 44,800 dollars for housing assistance and 44,800 dollars for other needs assistance (Federal Register notice of 29 September 2026). The Individual Assistance rule of 2024 added Serious Needs Assistance and Displacement Assistance; 206.119 as it now stands has no SBA loan application requirement.

registration.value: Calla Rourke, with Desmond Rourke. Registered 22 Jul 2026, inside the registration period, for the Harrowmere Valley floods (DR-9017).
218 Millrace Road, Harrowmere, owner-occupied since 2011. Flooded 12 to 14 Jul 2026.
A lake cabin at 9 Heron Landing, used on weekends and in summer. Also damaged.
Hearthguard homeowners policy HG-441, claim opened 15 Jul 2026. FEMA has the claim number and no settlement letter or denial letter from Hearthguard.
One car, flooded. No comprehensive auto coverage.
6 Aug 2026 (lodging) and 20 Aug 2026 (everything else). No appeal has been filed on either.
